sections.title: 1. Executive summary
sections.content:
Falak AI Solutions Co. (Riyadh, founded 2019, 42 full-time employees) is pleased to respond to the General Authority for Citizen Services' tender for a bilingual (Arabic/English) AI virtual assistant for citizen services. The assistant will serve the web portal, mobile app and WhatsApp, with handover to human agents.

Our core business is Arabic NLP and conversational AI, with AI model hosting in Saudi in-Kingdom cloud regions only. Two recent projects are directly comparable to this scope:
- P1, an Arabic/English customer-service chatbot for a Saudi retail bank (SAR 3.2 million, 2023-2024). It ran on web, mobile and WhatsApp with Najdi and Hijazi dialect support and handover to human agents. 61% of conversations were resolved without an agent and CSAT was 4.4/5.
- P2, a government services virtual assistant for a semi-government authority (SAR 4.8 million, 2024-2025). It handled citizen enquiries, was integrated with a case-management system, was hosted in-Kingdom and was NCA ECC compliant. It handled 1.2 million conversations in its first 6 months.

We hold the mandatory eligibility documents (Commercial Registration, Zakat, GOSI, Nitaqat, ISO/IEC 27001, and a 52% LCGPA-certified local content score against the 40% minimum). We also have 3 PMP-certified project managers and a 24/7 support and operations rota.

This is a first draft. Items not evidenced in our files are marked [TO CONFIRM] and listed in Section 7 for human review before submission.

[TO CONFIRM: the Zakat certificate (ZATCA-ZK-55821) expires 2026-12-05, four days after the 2026-12-01 deadline. Renewal should be started before submission.]

sections.title: 2. Understanding of requirements
sections.content:
The Authority requires a conversational AI assistant that:
- Is delivered on three channels: web portal, mobile app and WhatsApp (R15).
- Supports English and Arabic, including Modern Standard Arabic and Saudi dialects. Najdi and Hijazi are mandatory; Gulf and Southern dialects are desirable (R16, R22-R25).
- Handles about 400,000 enquiries per month, with human handover that carries full conversation context (R14).
- Integrates with the Authority's case-management system via REST APIs (R17).
- Includes an admin console for content updates and an analytics dashboard (R18, R19).
- Runs for 6 months of operation and support after go-live at 99.5% availability (R20, R21).
- Hosts all data, models and logs inside the Kingdom (R10), complies with NCA ECC (R11) and PDPL (R12), and is managed by a PMP-certified project manager (R13).

The contract runs 18 months: a 12-month build followed by 6 months of operation (R26). The estimated budget is SAR 6.5 million.

Administrative requirements:
- Eligibility: Commercial Registration, Zakat, GOSI, Nitaqat, ISO/IEC 27001 and local content of at least 40% (R1-R6).
- Experience: two conversational AI projects in the last five years, each above SAR 2 million, with client reference letters (R7-R9).
- Submission: technical and financial envelopes submitted separately (R29, R30), a bid bond of 1% of bid value valid for 90 days (R31), and a compliance matrix covering Sections 3 and 4 (R32).
- Deadlines: proposal by 2026-12-01 at 13:00 Riyadh time (R27); clarification questions by 2026-11-15 (R28).
- Evaluation: the technical proposal must score at least 65%. Technical carries 70% (experience 25%, methodology 25%, team 20%) and financial 30% (R33).

Scale observation: 400,000 enquiries per month is roughly double the average monthly volume of P2 (1.2 million conversations in its first 6 months, about 200,000 per month). We have no documented evidence of performance at the Authority's target volume. [TO CONFIRM: load and capacity evidence at about 400,000 enquiries per month.]

Questions we propose to raise with the Authority before 2026-11-15 (R28):
- The REST API specification of the case-management system.
- The SLA definition and measurement method for 99.5% availability.
- The expected handover context format.

sections.title: 3. Technical approach and methodology
sections.content:
Note: this section describes our proposed approach, which is a commitment to be validated by the delivery team. It is informed by the scope and results of P1 and P2. Specific technologies, architectures and tools are not named because they are not documented in the company files. [TO CONFIRM: solution architecture, product components and technology stack to be supplied by the technical lead.]

Proposed phasing of the 12-month build, then 6 months of operation (R26). [TO CONFIRM: detailed 12+6 month plan and milestones; no schedule evidence exists in the files.]

1. Mobilisation and discovery
- Confirm scope, channels, enquiry categories and the case-management integration with the Authority.
- Establish governance led by a PMP-certified project manager.

2. Conversation design and language
- Arabic-first conversation and interface design by our UX team.
- Arabic (Modern Standard Arabic, with Najdi and Hijazi dialects) and English support, building on P1's bilingual Najdi/Hijazi delivery. [TO CONFIRM: Modern Standard Arabic support is not explicitly stated for P1 or P2.]
- Gulf and Southern dialects are optional. [TO CONFIRM: no evidence in the files; decide whether to offer them.]

3. Channels
- Web portal, mobile app and WhatsApp, as delivered together in P1.

4. Integration
- Integration with the Authority's case-management system, building on our P2 integration with a case-management system. [TO CONFIRM: use of REST APIs is not stated in the P2 record.]

5. Human handover
- Escalation to human agents as delivered in P1. [TO CONFIRM: the transfer of full conversation context to the agent is not explicitly documented.]

6. Administration and analytics
- An admin console for content updates. [TO CONFIRM: no file documents this capability.]
- An analytics dashboard. We have data-platform and executive-dashboard experience (P4), but no conversational AI analytics dashboard is documented. [TO CONFIRM.]

7. Hosting, security and data protection
- Hosting entirely in in-Kingdom data centres (Riyadh and Jeddah regions), covering data, models and logs (R10). [TO CONFIRM: that logs, backups and any third-party services also remain in-Kingdom.]
- NCA ECC compliance. Our last ECC assessment was March 2026 (report ECC-2026-03), and P2 was ECC compliant.
- PDPL: a PDPL programme and an appointed DPO are in place. [TO CONFIRM: no certificate or audit evidence in the files.]

8. Testing, go-live and 6-month operation
- 6 months of operation and support after go-live, supported by our 24/7 operations rota (6 support and operations staff). [TO CONFIRM: support-contract evidence.]
- Target of 99.5% availability. [TO CONFIRM: no past SLA or availability record; the measurement method is to be agreed with the Authority.]

sections.title: 4. Relevant experience
sections.content:
Qualifying conversational AI projects (R7-R9), both within the last five years, above SAR 2,000,000, and supported by reference letters:

- P1. Arabic customer-service chatbot, regional Saudi retail bank (client name withheld), 2023-2024, SAR 3.2 million. Scope: bilingual Arabic/English chatbot on web, mobile and WhatsApp, with Najdi and Hijazi dialect support and handover to human agents. Results: 61% of conversations resolved without an agent; CSAT 4.4/5. Reference letter: yes. Relevance: the same channels, dialects and handover as this tender.

- P2. Government services virtual assistant, semi-government authority, 2024-2025, SAR 4.8 million. Scope: conversational AI for citizen enquiries, integrated with a case-management system, hosted in-Kingdom and NCA ECC compliant. Results: 1.2 million conversations in the first 6 months. Reference letter: yes. Relevance: the same citizen-services context, case-management integration, in-Kingdom hosting and ECC compliance.

Supporting projects:
- P3. Archive digitization and Arabic OCR, public university, 2022-2023, SAR 2.1 million. It digitised 1.8 million pages of Arabic documents and delivered a search portal. Reference letter: yes. It demonstrates Arabic language-processing depth, but is not a conversational AI project.
- P4. Municipal performance dashboard, municipality, 2021-2022, SAR 1.4 million. It delivered a data platform and executive dashboards. Reference letter: yes. It is relevant to the analytics dashboard requirement (R19).

Project P5 (contract-document classification, SAR 0.9 million, 2025) has a pending reference letter and is not relied upon.

[TO CONFIRM: that the P1 and P2 reference letters are current and acceptable to the Authority, since the P1 client name is withheld. Also confirm which project figures can be disclosed.]

shortlist.reason: Bilingual AI citizen-services assistant closely matches past projects P1 and P2 (SAR 4.8M, in-Kingdom, NCA ECC); SAR 6.5M is within the SAR 10M comfort limit and the deadline of 2026-12-01 allows about a month.
Archive digitization with AI data extraction matches P3 (1.8M pages of Arabic OCR, including handwritten) and the SAR 3.8M value is comfortably in range.
Contract clause extraction with NLP matches P5, but the deadline of 2026-10-20 has already passed (today is 2026-10-30).
Arabic speech-to-text falls within Arabic NLP and voice assistants, but no past project covers speech recognition specifically, so the gap should be checked in the full documents.

Data analytics platform fits P4 (municipal dashboards) and the data-platform capability, but at SAR 9M it is near the SAR 10M comfort limit and the smart-city scope may include IoT elements the company does not do.
A radiology triage system is a regulated medical device, and the company holds no SFDA MDMA or ISO 13485 and has no clinical staff.
Laptop hardware supply is outside the company's scope, which covers no hardware.
Office furniture supply is outside the company's scope, which is AI, NLP, OCR and data platforms.
Cleaning and maintenance of schools is facility maintenance, which the company explicitly does not do.
School construction at SAR 28M is outside the company's scope and far above its SAR 10M comfort limit, and no contractor classification is held.
